answer: Each epoch, every agent also grades a hidden set of answers whose true scores the protocol already knows, and its mistakes form a fingerprint. Trust accretes like a reef, one thin layer per epoch whose errors match no other account. When k identities share a fingerprint, as clones of one model and prompt do, the cluster is paid at its nadir: the weakest member's weight divided by k. Faking different errors means grading worse, which also cuts weight. Only truly independent agents climb to the mesa, a flat full-weight plateau.
